8. Housing Services  
 
1. Summary 
This Report is produced to give an overview of the delivery of the Housing Capital 
Programme and Housing Services at Westmeath County Council. The Report also covers the 
provision, maintenance and management of housing stock and the housing supports 
available for those who need them.  
The Report covers the following areas: 
Housing Capital Delivery 
Construction & Planned Delivery 
Affordable Housing Programme 
Croí Cónaithe Scheme 
Acquisitions & Social Leasing 
Traveller Specific Accommodation 
Housing Support  
Housing Need Assessment 
RAS, Leasing, HAP and Housing Allocations 
Housing Adaptation Grants 
Private Rented Housing Standards  
Local Authority Home Loan Scheme, Mortgage to Rent and the Tenant Purchase Scheme 
Housing Maintenance and Retrofit Scheme 
Homeless Services

8. Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant 
The Croí Cónaithe (Towns) Fund in the form of the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant 
provides further opportunities for people to live in towns and villages in Westmeath 
through the provision of a grant to support the refurbishment of vacant properties, with 
priority given to areas where the level of vacancy or dereliction is high. 
 
As of 30th April 2026: 
• Number of applications –435 
• Funding Issued –130 
• Approved (Invoices received and at the legal charge stage) –9 
• Approved in Principle (1st Inspection complete and works approved) – 152 
• Further Information requested – 96 
• Rejected/withdrawn – 48 
 
The process for applying for the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant moved to an online 
portal from the 05/01/2026 providing a more streamlined process for grant applicants.

9. Second Hand Acquisitions Programme 
Confirmation of the Second-Hand Acquisition Budget for 2026 was announced on 24th 
February, with a budget of €373 million announced nationally. The allocation for 
Westmeath County Council is €2,400,000  - €1,700,00 for local authority acquisitions, which 
is fully committed to date. The Balance of €700,000 is ringfenced for CAS Acquisitions.  
 
Housing Circular 07/2026 was subsequently issued on 27th February 2026 and outlines the 
arrangements for the Social Housing Acquisition Programme in 2026. The funding for 2026 
will support acquisitions under the following categories: 
 
• Exiting households from homeless services 
• Persons with disabilities, older persons and care leavers requiring urgent housing 
responses 
• Tenancy sustainment (tenant-in-situ)

Ongoing discussions with Developers/Property Owners/AHBs with regard to support for

Kingscourt, Castlepollard - Currently liaising with developer to deliver 9 units via Part V 
agreement.

agreement. 
 
Cornamaddy Athlone – Currently liaising with the developer to deliver a further 3 units via 
Turnkey arrangements. WCC acquired 8 Part V units in the same development in late 2025.  
 
 
 
 
Saunders Bridge, Mullingar - Currently liaising with developer to deliver 9 units via Part V 
agreement.

Bellview Grove, Mullingar- – Currently liaising with the developer to deliver one further unit

11. Traveller Accommodation 
Blackberry Lane, Athlone - Redevelopment of the site to include 41 new units. Stage 2 
approval received from the Department in May 2023. This project is currently at 
preplanning stage. The Traveller Accommodation Programme 2025-2029 was adopted by 
the Elected Members at the December Council meeting. 
 
The Traveller Accommodation Programme target for 2025 for all social housing supports is 
26 households. 20 properties have been allocated to Traveller families. In addition, 10 
properties were offered but refused and 2 families have found HAP properties. 
 
 
12. Housing Supports and Services 
The Housing Section continues to provide a wide range of Housing Supports to Social 
Housing Applicants to Social Housing Tenants.  Westmeath County Council is currently in the 
process of completing the Summary of Social Housing Assessments (SSHA) under S.21 of the 
Housing (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2009 by the deadline of 3rd November 2025.  
 
 
13. Housing Maintenance 
Managing housing maintenance county wide, ensuring value for money while adhering to 
response times set in Tenant handbook. The Housing Department continues to engage with 
the Department regarding various funding programmes.
